public_rationale: The annual-loss figures reach tens of billions on a reported net-loss basis: Anthropic disclosed $42.0 billion for 2025, and Ars Technica reported nearly $39 billion for OpenAI [e1, e2]. Anthropic's total includes $34.3 billion in fair-value changes, while OpenAI's includes a large valuation-related charge [e1, e2]. Ars Technica separately reports OpenAI's 2025 operating loss as $20.92 billion, illustrating why the loss measure matters [e2]. These records do not establish lifetime recovery of hyperscaler GPU spending [e1, e2]. S&P Global's August 27, 2026 outlook forecasts improving monetization but documents neither verified recovery nor a closed investment lifecycle for a defined trillion-plus GPU investment [e3]. The forecast that hyperscalers will never recover that spending therefore remains unresolved [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: The reported net and operating losses do not settle an unspecified loss measure or isolate losses attributable to GPU rentals [e1, e2].
OpenAI's figures are secondary reporting on financial statements [e2].
The infrastructure outlook does not establish a defined trillion-plus GPU purchase cohort, its attributable cumulative returns or final recoveries [e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Anthropic and OpenAI lose tens of billions a year, and hyperscalers will never recoup their trillion-plus GPU spending.

statement.excerpt: AI startups and enterprise customers pay Anthropic and OpenAI on a per-million token rate (losing money in the process) so that Anthropic and OpenAI can rent GPUs from hyperscalers (losing tens of billions of dollars a year) so that hyperscalers can buy a trillion or more dollars’ worth of GPUs (putting them in such a hole that they’ll never, ever be able to make the money back).
statement.document_title: The More You Buy, The More You Lose

from_speaker: losing tens of billions of dollars a year
a trillion or more dollars’ worth of GPUs
they’ll never, ever be able to make the money back
our_interpretation: This is a compound claim: a present annual-loss observation and an indefinite forecast about recovery of hyperscaler GPU investment. The forecast determines the overall horizon.
For the loss clause, I use calendar 2025, the latest completed annual period before publication. I do not annualize a later half-year figure.
I read tens of billions as at least USD20 billion annually for the two labs collectively. The wording could also be read as applying separately to each.
The source does not specify net loss, operating loss or cash burn. Those measures must not be substituted for one another.
Making the money back means cumulative attributable returns after operating costs and recoveries covering the relevant GPU purchase cost. Company-wide revenue alone would not demonstrate recovery.

The contract metric_scope describes the forecast's GPU investment. The separate loss clause concerns Anthropic and OpenAI, USD billions, realized annual flows for January–December 2025, with an unspecified accounting basis.
No deadline, fixed GPU investment cohort or exhaustive list of hyperscalers is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable annual figures establish the lab-loss assertion, and a closed investment lifecycle establishes that the relevant trillion-plus GPU spending was not recovered and can generate no further recoveries. Present losses or slow returns alone cannot establish never.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable annual figures refute the loss assertion, or verified cumulative attributable net returns and recoveries cover the relevant GPU investment. Because the financial basis is unspecified, a supported or contradicted score requires resolving that basis first.

evidence.locator: Risk Factors, page 64; auditor's report, pages F-2–F-3
evidence.explanation: The surrounding disclosure reports a USD42.0 billion 2025 net loss, including USD34.3 billion of fair-value changes. This establishes a substantial accounting loss but does not identify GPU rental losses or settle the speaker's unspecified loss measure.

evidence.locator: Gotta spend money to make money, first paragraph
evidence.explanation: The report distinguishes OpenAI's net loss from operating losses and describes a large accounting charge. It is secondary reporting on audited company statements, not evidence that the entire loss arose from GPU rental.

This competing outlook anticipates improving monetization. It is not realized investment recovery, and the report's broad capital-expenditure measure cannot establish trillion-plus GPU spending or its lifetime return.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Establish comparable calendar-2025 losses for both labs on an explicit accounting basis. Define the hyperscalers and GPU investment cohort. Verified cumulative attributable returns after operating costs, plus recoveries, covering the purchase cost would contradict 'never.' Support would require final retirement or disposal and closure of all economic interests, with total returns below cost and no possible further recoveries.
